headline: The head of MI5 warns that terrorists could use AI to improve attacks with drones and to get help with biological weapons, and says his service has opened an AI threat assessment centre.
score_reason: Pool score kept: an official warning from the head of the UK's domestic security service and a new AI assessment unit, though the bioweapon risk is described as not yet real.
importance_line: People in Britain and anyone relying on its banks, hospitals and airports are the audience for this warning, and the new AI centre shows the threat is being taken seriously, but McCallum himself says the bioweapon risk is not yet real and the coverage describes no specific AI-enabled plot.
summary: The Independent reports that Sir Ken McCallum, director general of MI5, Britain's domestic security service, said in his annual speech on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 that MI5 has "caught terrorists seeking to exploit AI" to improve reconnaissance and attack methods, with AI-enabled drones adding "a new twist", and that his greatest concern is AI's potential to "change the stakes" on bioweapons. He announced that MI5 launched an AI Threat Assessment Centre this year and said the bioweapon risk is "not yet manifest"; this follows our 11 Oct 2026 edition, which carried The Sunday Times report that the heads of MI5, MI6 and GCHQ told the cabinet that AI could become one of Britain's biggest security threats.
notes: Politico original (HTTP 403) unreadable; text read on The Independent and cross-checked with the BBC article carried by Yahoo News Australia. Follow-up of the 11 Oct 2026 edition item (The Sunday Times, spy chiefs warn cabinet).
